import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_bmi_processed.csv')

# Define the variables of interest
X = df[['DISSAVED', 'SAMESAVE']]
y = df['BMI']

# Add a constant to the predictor variables
X = sm.add_constant(X)

# Fit the linear regression model
model = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()

# Print the model summary

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import pearsonr, ttest_ind

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_bmi_processed.csv')

# Calculate Pearson correlation between DISSAVED and BMI
corr_dissaved, p_dissaved = pearsonr(df['DISSAVED'], df['BMI'])

# Calculate Pearson correlation between SAMESAVE and BMI
corr_samesave, p_samesave = pearsonr(df['SAMESAVE'], df['BMI'])

# Perform t-test to compare BMI between DISSAVED and non-DISSAVED groups
ttest_dissaved = ttest_ind(df[df['DISSAVED'] == 1]['BMI'], df[df['DISSAVED'] == 0]['BMI'])

# Perform t-test to compare BMI between SAMESAVE and non-SAMESAVE groups
ttest_samesave = ttest_ind(df[df['SAMESAVE'] == 1]['BMI'], df[df['SAMESAVE'] == 0]['BMI'])

corr_dissaved, p_dissaved, corr_samesave, p_samesave, ttest_dissaved, ttest_samesave
